rationale: The revised fixed experiment for the replay-completion question has been executed (receipt e82594cc274340f0a961608cda519e00). It reproduces the earlier block and measures the bound with a smaller legal MaxAppendEntries, so this batch replaces the previous account with one that cites both receipts and no longer treats the proportional bound as source-derived only.

interpretations.rationale: Two executions of the same fixed experiment agree. Receipt e82594cc274340f0a961608cda519e00 first reruns the original pair: event 16 records a prefix with 9000 applied commands, log_last_index 9002, staged_commit_index 9001, snapshot_index 0 and 141 replay batches at MaxAppendEntries 64; the flag-on restart admitted by event 17 did not return from NewRaft within 8000ms (event 18, new_raft_returned false) and the sampled stack again names processLogs at raft.go:1346 called from restoreFromCommittedLogs at api.go:753 called from NewRaft, while the flag-off restart of the same shape returned in 5ms (event 21) and became leader (event 22). Receipt 3d04552f58e548b0ae089192392b564f recorded the same outcome with return in 1ms, so the block reproduces across two independent executions with different addresses. The revision then measures the bound: events 23 and 27 record two prefixes built the same way at MaxAppendEntries 16 with 1501 and 3001 replayed entries, that is 94 and 188 batches; the below-bound restart (comparison 0, event 25) returned from NewRaft in 0ms, and the above-bound restart (comparison 1, witness event 29) did not return, with the stack sample naming the same replay frames. Because the two cases share the flag, the batch size, the store machinery and the harness, and differ only in replay volume, the boundary between them measures the completion bound as 128 batches times MaxAppendEntries (2048 entries at 16, 8192 at the default 64) rather than a fixed amount of log. Source side, the mechanism is settled and makes the wait permanent rather than slow: processLogs delivers each batch through a select whose only other case is shutdownCh (raft.go:1302-1312), fsmMutateCh is created with capacity 128 (api.go:560), and its only consumer runFSM is started by api.go:636-638 after the replay returns; the replay needs ceil((commitIndex - lastApplied)/MaxAppendEntries) sends, so once the count passes 128 the 129th send waits for a consumer that cannot exist until the blocked call finishes, with no timeout and no reachable way to close shutdownCh because the caller never receives the object. Defect statement, now scoped to the measured bound: with Config.RestoreCommittedLogs enabled, NewRaft cannot complete startup whenever the committed log it replays exceeds 128*MaxAppendEntries entries above the restored snapshot index; at the default MaxAppendEntries of 64 that is 8192 entries, and it is proportionally smaller for any smaller legal value, as measured at 16. The failure is startup liveness, not a wrong decision: the node never begins participating, so a single-voter group stays down and a larger group permanently loses one member.

knowledge.assertion: Each batch is delivered with a select between a send on fsmMutateCh and shutdownCh, so a full channel with no consumer waits indefinitely.
fsmMutateCh has capacity 128 and its consumer runFSM starts only after the startup replay returns.
The replay range above the snapshot sets the batch count, and the automatic snapshot cadence is the only bound on that range in a default deployment.
With the flag on, lastApplied is set to the persisted commit index before the replay, so the replay range spans the committed log above the snapshot.

counterevidence: The block itself is evidenced by non-return within an 8000ms window plus one stack sample per blocked case (events 18 and 29). The permanence argument does not rest on those samples: the source shows no timeout, a single consumer started only after the blocked call returns, and an escape requiring an object the caller has not received. The flag-off control returns in 1ms and 5ms across the two receipts (events 21 in each), so the wait is not the cost of the work.

The measured bound comes from one batch size: the below and above cases both ran at MaxAppendEntries 16, while the earlier pair shows blocking at 141 batches at MaxAppendEntries 64. No registration was run between 94 and 128 batches, so the exact boundary is bracketed rather than binary-searched, and the arithmetic form of the bound is still supported by the source rather than by the measurement alone.

With the default SnapshotThreshold of 8192 equal to the default bound, a default node blocks only when its committed range above the snapshot overshoots the bound; both the earlier and the revised cases raised SnapshotThreshold, a legal Config field, so how often a default deployment crosses the bound is not measured.

The below-bound restart returned from NewRaft but had not elected itself one second later (event 26: final_state Follower, leader_observed false, commit_index 1501). That is not a failure of this question's predicate, and it is also not explained by this receipt, which records no configuration operands; the sibling investigation's mechanism predicts an empty tracked configuration for exactly this restart, and that attribution is an open direction rather than an observation here.

The replay range comes from the caller-side store's persisted commit index, and the harness uses a test store whose staging is not atomic with its log writes, so the size of the range in a production deployment is a caller property that this receipt does not constrain.
limitations: Both prefixes are single-voter in-memory clusters over an in-memory commit-tracking log store, with SnapshotThreshold raised so no automatic snapshot moves the replay bound; no multi-node cluster is exercised, so the member loss caused by a node that cannot start is argued rather than observed.

The blocked NewRaft call is abandoned in a separate goroutine so the test can complete; that is a harness choice, not a repair, and it means the harness itself never observes the process-level consequence of a real startup hang.
Both executions use one wait length (8000ms) and one prefix shape per case; schedule variation beyond two runs is not characterized.
The bound is measured at two batch sizes (16 and 64) and one replay per side, so the claim is a measured threshold bracket plus a source-derived formula, not a scan of the boundary.
interpretations.joint_history: Both receipts belong to this investigation and are compatible as successive observations of the same prefix machinery: 3d04552f58e548b0ae089192392b564f is the predecessor fixed experiment, and e82594cc274340f0a961608cda519e00 is its revision, whose harness is a strict superset (the two original 9000-entry cases unchanged, plus the two MaxAppendEntries-16 cases). The original pair uses identical inputs in both harnesses and emits the same event names with the same operands apart from independently generated random addresses and observed return latencies, so the earlier receipt contributes reproducibility of the block and of the flag-off control, while the bound pair exists only in the later receipt.
